comment: Read at commit f845b65 (AFHawthorn/HawthornLabs), the tip of master. Seven commits carry 2.0.2. The installed manifest is byte-identical from e96f41c onward, which rules out the two earlier ones. Between the three that remain, the installed build settles it: it reads the channels byte twice, once gating the sine write and once gating the trigger write, which is the split made in 84fbf87; the only later commit, f845b65, widens planetDur from long to long long, which changes nothing on arm64 where long is already 64-bit. The panel carries only four pieces of lettering - the title, Speed, reset and the brand - so none of the eighteen output jacks is named on it; the planet names exist only in configOutput. The word reset labels both the input jack and the button below it, so both lines say which. Every configInput and configOutput is called once with the matching enum. Widget order does follow enum order, but the two enum runs interleave on the panel: the nine trigger jacks are outputs 0 to 8 and the nine sine jacks outputs 9 to 17, and each planet's pair sits together, so reading down a column alternates between the two runs. Two things the maker's README does not say. The phase is advanced only on every other sample (line 84, counter % 2 == 0) while the increment at line 87 is computed for a full sample, so every LFO runs at half the stated rate and every trigger pulse lasts twice its nominal 10ms. And the README gives Earth's year as 365.25 days while the constants in the source give 365.2; the source figure is the one in the lines, and the other eight periods in the README agree exactly with the planetDur array. A PulseGenerator is only stepped while its own jack is patched (line 96), so a trigger output that has been left unpatched across a wrap emits the remainder of that pulse when a cable is put in. The six lamps are not ParamWidgets and cannot be clicked, so they get a Note rather than a line. The module has no menu of its own.
